summary: We demonstrate a 99.62% fidelity CZ gate between two multimode P-mon superconducting qubits coupled via their flux-tunable mediator modes, achieving ZZ-type crosstalk suppressed to 3.6 kHz through mode-selective coupling that keeps computational qubits isolated. The gate exploits qubit-state-dependent frequency shifts from cross-Kerr interactions ($\alpha_{\mathcal{AB}} \approx -164$ and $-108$ MHz) to generate an entangling phase without linear qubit-qubit exchange.
motivation: Scaling superconducting quantum processors requires maintaining high coherence times while suppressing always-on ZZ interactions that induce correlated errors; standard transmon architectures using capacitive couplers suffer from frequency crowding and crosstalk in the straddling regime.
method: Two P-mons are coupled via an intermediate 8.143 GHz bus resonator connected only to island 3, establishing a $g_{\mathcal{BB}}/2\pi = 11.7$ MHz mediator-mediator coupling while leaving qubit modes ($\omega_{\mathcal{A}}/2\pi \approx 4.5$ GHz) decoupled; we drive the $|0,0\rangle_\mathcal{B} \leftrightarrow |-\rangle_{00}$ transition selectively with 180 ns HD-DRAG pulses to accumulate an entangling phase via the cyclic Bloch sphere trajectory.
result: CZ gate fidelity of $99.62(4)\%$ measured via interleaved randomized benchmarking with 180 ns HD-DRAG pulses; residual ZZ interaction $\zeta_{ZZ} = 3.6(5)$ kHz at the gate operation point, with qubit coherence times $T_1 = 139(18)$ and $141(13)$ µs and mediator dephasing $T_2 = 5.2(6)$ µs limiting performance at short durations.
